doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Playing, records and the Hyman album
title: The Dick Hyman, Hinton and Pizzarelli album and co-writing credit
summary: Monk praises the album's opening hi-hat track; Butch recalls Hyman asking for a Basie-style rhythm start and sharing co-writing credit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Milt Hinton, what a team, Urbie Green, Bucky Pizzarelli, Joe Temperley, Frank Wess, Joe Wilder, and Dick Hyman charts. And actually this one I would have on my desert island list.

That’s a good one. I have to tell you I forgot about that really. But that is a very good album specifically because of the giants that are all on there that I’m just trying to keep time for, and not get in their way. They play so beautifully, they play so musically, they play so, just magnificent.

Yes. And the CD, the recording starts with just a quartet, no horns, and I believe it’s off- the-cuff, and Dick Hyman sets up the tempo much like Basie would. And you come in. And all you’re playing is the hi-hat and the stand. I mean you probably don’t remember it but it made such an impression on me because it’s just such like a tick-tick-a-tick-tick. And it’s so hip, and you’ve got all this room to go into and I just think it’s like a drum lesson right there.

Well thank you very much. Thank you. I remember now, Dick Hyman was so brilliant, he said, “Listen fellas,” I remember this strangely enough, I don’t know why but I do. He looked at us before we started recording and said, “Listen fellas, I want to start off, we’re going to make something up. It’s going to be the lead-off on the album and we’ll make this up.” He said, “Now Butch, you and Milt have worked with Count Basie before.” “Yeah.” He said, “Give me a Basie style tempo and Bucky, you do your Freddie Green thing” so the rhythm section was all ready to go, and so we jumped in and we said, “Okay here’s what we’re going to do” and then Dick started to jam over the top of that and then the rest of it you know exactly what happened. Dick Hyman is such a gentleman that when the album was released he sent all of us a note and he said — me and Milt and Bucky, he said, “Because you set it up and you guys were the ones who came up with the Basie ideas, I’m giving you co-writing rights on this one so that you’ll also get a little bit
of extra change for all the albums that are sold,” because we were listed as co-writers. He’s a gentleman.
I can confirm that, I’m looking at it right now, “From the Age of Swing, Hyman, Hinton, Pizzarelli and Miles. That’s awesome.
For ideas, and because the maestro, Maestro Hyman, had suggested that we come up with some ideas for rhythm in a Basie style.
